name: opaque-library
description: A call into pure-Python library code is one step, not a tour of its internals.

not_applicable.javascript: JavaScript's standard library is native code, so a call into it has no frames to hide in the first place. `JSON.stringify` never enters instrumented source, which means the property this case tests holds trivially and cannot be observed: there is no library frame to report. A JavaScript case worth writing here would need an imported package, which is a different thing to test and belongs with module support.
not_applicable.java: The Java adapter keeps library code out by telling the JVM never to report it: `java.*`, `javax.*`, `jdk.*`, `sun.*` and `com.sun.*` are excluded from stepping and from method entry, so a call into the standard library costs one step and generates no frames. The property this case tests therefore holds by construction and leaves nothing to observe -- there is no library frame to report, because one is never created. Testing it for Java would mean asserting the absence of something that cannot occur.
